standard_prerequisites.name: Super Yangian and its RTT presentation
standard_prerequisites.statement: For the general linear Lie superalgebra gl_{M|N} over C the Yangian Y(gl_{M|N}) is the associative Z_2-graded algebra with generators T_ij^(r) for r at least 1, whose generating series T_ij(u) satisfy the RTT relation; the inverse matrix series is written T'_ij(u) and the antipode is written S. The author sets all of this up at source lines 169-320, which are retained in the material, so nothing in the counted proof depends on an outside convention.
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the algebra, its generators, the series T_ij(u) and T'_ij(u) and the antiautomorphism tau from which the operator Q is built.

standard_prerequisites.name: Formal power series in u^{-1} and the rational R-matrix
standard_prerequisites.statement: All series are formal in the variable u^{-1} with coefficients in the Yangian, and the rational R-matrix R(u) together with its twisted inverse R-hat_S(u) = 1 + Q(u-M+N)^{-1} is used through the identities recorded at source lines 249-308, which are retained in the material.
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the identities (3.0), (3.3), (3.52) and (pop) that the counted proof quotes when it forms Q, R-hat_S and the three-leg computation.

core_obligations: Introduce the element Q = (id tensor tau)(P) with one-dimensional image and compute Q^2 = (M-N)Q and the inverse of (id tensor tau)(R(u)) as 1 + Q(u-M+N)^{-1} (source lines 888-907).

Derive from the RTT relation the equality (R-hat_S(u-v) tensor 1) T_1(u) T'_2(v) = T'_2(v) T_1(u) (R-hat_S(u-v) tensor 1) and evaluate its residue at u = v+M-N to get (Q tensor 1) T_1(v+M-N) T'_2(v) = T'_2(v) T_1(v+M-N) (Q tensor 1) (source lines 909-921).

Conclude from the one-dimensionality of the image of Q that either side of that equality equals Q tensor Z(v) for a unique series Z(v) in v^{-1}, and identify the two displayed identities with the left and right sides (source lines 923-932).
Show that the leading term of Z(u) is 1 and that every coefficient has Z_2-degree 0 (source lines 934-937).

Prove centrality of every coefficient by the three-leg computation with the projector Q_23, using the identity Q_23 R-hat_S_13(u+M-N) R_12(u) = (1-u^{-2}) Q_23 and the display (3.666666) (source lines 941-976).

proof_roadmap.step: Define Q, compute Q^2 and invert (id tensor tau)(R(u)).
Rescale the RTT relation and take its residue at u = v+M-N.
Extract the series Z(v) from the one-dimensional image of Q and identify the two identities.
Read off the leading term 1 and the Z_2-degree 0.
Prove centrality of all coefficients with the three-leg Q_23 computation.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is Proposition 3.1 at source lines 877-886, label zu: there is a formal power series Z(u) in u^{-1} with leading term 1 and central coefficients such that for all i, j the two displayed sums, the sum of T_kj(u+M-N) T'_ik(u) and the sum of T'_kj(u) T_ik(u+M-N), both equal delta_ij Z(u). The proof at source lines 888-977 must first build the rank-one operator Q = (id tensor tau)(P), compute Q^2 = (M-N)Q and invert (id tensor tau)(R(u)) as 1 + Q(u-M+N)^{-1}, then take the residue of the rescaled RTT relation at u = v+M-N; the non-routine step is the conclusion that either side of the resulting identity must equal Q tensor Z(v) because Q has one-dimensional image, which is what produces the series Z(v) instead of only a relation among generators. Centrality is a second, separate computation at source lines 941-977 with the projector Q_23 and the identity Q_23 R-hat_S_13(u+M-N) R_12(u) = (1-u^{-2}) Q_23, where the scalar factor is not invertible as a formal series and the conclusion has to be drawn from the two displays rather than by dividing. Both computations are self-contained once the paper's own RTT machinery is available, so the card is rated H2.

compared.difference: Same source, different proposition: the counted public unit of doi:10.3842/SIGMA.2020.112 is Theorem 2.8 (label T18, statement at source lines 849-850 with the counted proof at 844-850), the isomorphism of the enveloping algebra of the current Lie superalgebra with the associated graded Yangian, whose obligation is injectivity of the current-algebra map. The present card counts Proposition 3.1 (label zu, source lines 877-886) with its proof at 888-977, the construction of the central series Z(u) and the two RTT-type identities it satisfies; it is a different proposition in a later section and it asserts centrality of a specific series, not an associated-graded isomorphism.

editorial_notes: The counted unit is Proposition 3.1 at source lines 877-886, source label zu, with the proof environment that begins on the next line at 888-977; the pairing is the ordinary adjacent one. The printed number is fixed by initial_counters so that every retained item keeps its original number: the source has the Introduction as section 1, so starting the counter at 1 makes the retained Definition of the Yangian section 2 (with its Proposition 2.1) and the Centre of the Yangian section 3, where the counted proposition prints as Proposition 3.1 exactly as in the published article.

The retained definition passages at source lines 169-351 and 368-422 are the author's own Section 1 on the definition of the Yangian: the graded tensor conventions, the generators and their defining relations, the permutation operator P, the R-matrix with (3.52), the series T(u) and T_p(u), Propositions 2.1 and 2.2 with their proofs, the antiautomorphism tau of End C^{M|N} defined at line 368, Proposition 2.3 with its proof, and the series T^S(u) at line 414. The counted proof uses tau in its first line through the operator Q, so both passages are retained; they carry the section heading of the source and are context, not a second counted proposition.

The context span at 863-876 is the opening of the Centre of the Yangian section, including the author's remark that the description of the centre comes from computing the square of the antipodal mapping. No retained passage was altered.

The retained preamble reproduces the author's macro and theorem declaration block verbatim from source lines 9-71, including the same theorem environment names the SIGMA publisher class declares; the publisher class itself is not installed on the assembly host, so the wrapper class amsart is used and the equation counter is still tied to the section counter as in the source.

The retained bibliography carries exactly the one work cited by the retained text (Nazarov, Quantum Berezinian and the classical Capelli identity), copied verbatim from the source's own reference list.
